head: 5551601f25d80340bf9505d225270593013f16d9
title: Vectorize DCG calculation in retrieval evaluation
body:
## Change

Vectorize the discount calculation in InformationRetrievalEvaluator.compute_dcg_at_k. The evaluator currently calls NumPy's scalar log2 once per relevance entry and accumulates each term in Python, for every query and NDCG cutoff. Computing the discount vector and reduction together removes that per-entry Python work. Dense, sparse and multi-vector retrieval evaluators share this implementation.

Empty and non-positive cutoffs retain their zero result. Relevance inputs remain unmodified, and NumPy's dtype promotion preserves extended-precision inputs.

## Validation and benchmark

The successful DCG jobs in [this exact-base validation run](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43921700020) compare base `9ac7fdb4` with candidate `5551601f` on CPU with PyTorch **2.6.0** and **2.14.1**. All **85 new compatibility tests pass on both revisions**. Candidate tests plus the existing dense, sparse and multi-vector retrieval suites produce **103 passes and 2 CUDA skips** in each environment. All pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` pass.

The [reproducible benchmark](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/blob/d52e86f7b80cc9c660026e6403c2b7e9d32ca901/.validation/st-ir-dcg-benchmark.py) times the public compute_metrics method on precomputed rankings: 200 queries, 20 relevant documents per query, all six metric families, and every cutoff through the corpus size. It includes ranking sort and all metric calculations. Embedding and retrieval are outside the timed region. One warmup precedes five timed repetitions.

| PyTorch 2.14.1 CPU input | Before median | After median | Ratio |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 100 documents/query, 7 cutoffs | 65.94 ms | 27.25 ms | 2.42× |
| 1,000 documents/query, 9 cutoffs | 462.08 ms | 125.88 ms | 3.67× |

The independent PyTorch 2.6.0 runner measured 2.48× and 3.63×, respectively. Every returned metric at every cutoff agrees within `1e-13`; DCG tests also compare against a scalar math.fsum reference with graded relevances, short inputs and float32/float64 arrays.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex helped with investigation, implementation, compatibility tests and benchmarking.
